## Description or Purpose

Show differences in concentrations for individual metabolites as function of proliferation and subtype.

### Background

### Data sources

-   Cleaned, preprocessed, normalized, scaled metabolomics data
    -   Rates from Figure 2
    -   Intracellular concentrations from Figure 1
-   Metadata on cell line phenotypes

### Analysis plan

Build a plot for each metabolite, where x = proliferation, y = metabolite, and color is subtype.

#### Custom functions

```{r}
pivot_longer_metabolomics <- function(metabolomics) {
  metabolomics |>
    rownames_to_column("metabolite") |>
    pivot_longer(!metabolite, names_to = "cell_line", values_to = "value")
  
}
transpose_metabolomics <- function(metabolomics) {
  # From metabolites in rownames and cells in columns to 
  # cells in rownames and metabolites to columns
  metabolomics |>
    pivot_longer_metabolomics() |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = metabolite, values_from = value) |>
    column_to_rownames("cell_line")
}
```


#### Statistics per metabolite

The code in this section `Statistics per metabolite` is adapted from Leegwater et al 2025 ( "code\biology_manuscript_files_and_figures\Calculations_to_get_all_data_for_all_figures_after_peerreview.qmd") Figure 4, DOI: 10.1016/j.bbalip.2025.159679.


```{r}
#| eval: false
get_proliferation_metadata <- function(cell_line_metadata) {
  ## Filter to keep only cell lines for which we have proliferation rates
  proliferation_metadata <- cell_line_metadata |>
    dplyr::select(cell_line, Subtype_4_categories, ProliferationRate) |>
    filter(!is.na(ProliferationRate))
}

create_design_prol_subtype <- function(proliferation_metadata) {
  # Create a design object
  design <- model.matrix(
    ~ 0 + proliferation_metadata$Subtype_4_categories + 
      proliferation_metadata$ProliferationRate +
      proliferation_metadata$Subtype_4_categories:proliferation_metadata$ProliferationRate
  )
  
  rownames(design) <- proliferation_metadata$cell_line
  colnames(design) <- str_replace_all(colnames(design), "proliferation_metadata\\$", "")
  colnames(design) <- str_replace_all(colnames(design), "Subtype_4_categories", "")
  colnames(design) <- str_replace_all(colnames(design), "-like", "")
  colnames(design) <- str_replace_all(colnames(design), ":", ".") # needed for contrast fits
  return(design)
}
filter_metabolomics_prol <- function(metabolomics, cell_lines) {
  # Keep only cell lines for which we have proliferation rates
  dataset <- metabolomics |>
    select(any_of(cell_lines))
}
```

### Load data
Build a plot for each metabolite, where x = proliferation, y = metabolite, and color is subtype.

```{r}
# Metadata on cell line names
cell_line_metadata <- read_csv(here("data/Cell_line_metadata.csv"))
dim(cell_line_metadata)
head(cell_line_metadata)

# Change dashes in cell line names into dots to match preprocessed data
cell_line_metadata <- cell_line_metadata |>
  mutate(cell_line = str_replace_all(group, "-", "."))

# Load data
data_dir <- "data"
omics_datasets <- list(
  "amines"                  = read_csv(here(data_dir, "figure_1/amines.csv")) |>
    column_to_rownames("amine_metabolite"),
  "polar metabolomics"      = read_csv(here(data_dir, "figure_1/polar.csv")) |>
    column_to_rownames("polar_metabolite"),
  "metabolite rates minmax" = read_csv(here(data_dir, "figure_2/metabolite_rates_scaled_minmax.csv")) |>
    column_to_rownames("metabolite")
)

# Keep only metadata for measured cell lines
measured_cell_lines <- lapply(omics_datasets, colnames) |>
  unlist() |>
  unique()

dim(cell_line_metadata)
cell_line_metadata <- filter(cell_line_metadata, cell_line %in% measured_cell_lines)
dim(cell_line_metadata)
```

### Figure

#### Build plot

Boxplot is based on Leegwater et al. 2024, DOI:10.1002/cem.3636 -> script All_figures.Rmd

X axis adapted from # Source - https://stackoverflow.com/a/60650595 Posted by jan-glx, modified by community. See post 'Timeline' for change history. Retrieved 2026-10-15, License - CC BY-SA 4.0

```{r}
violin_metabolite_plot <- function(metabolomics, ylab = "scaled metabolite") {
  df_plot <- metabolomics |>
    pivot_longer_metabolomics() |>
    left_join(cell_line_metadata, by = "cell_line") |>
    # only plot when proliferation data is available
    filter(!is.na(ProliferationRate))
  p <- df_plot |>
    ggplot(aes(x = Subtype_4_categories, y = value, fill = Subtype_4_categories)) +
      geom_violin() +
      geom_boxplot(position=position_dodge(1), width=0.2, fill = "white") +
      scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90)) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = color_legend_Subtype) +
      labs(y = ylab, x = "Cell line subtype") +
      facet_wrap(~metabolite) +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  return(p)
}
```

```{r}
scatter_metabolite_plot <- function(metabolomics, ylab = "scaled metabolite") {
  df_plot <- metabolomics |>
    pivot_longer_metabolomics() |>
    left_join(cell_line_metadata, by = "cell_line") |>
    # only plot when proliferation data is available
    filter(!is.na(ProliferationRate))
  p <- df_plot |>
    ggplot(aes(x = ProliferationRate, y = value, color = Subtype_4_categories)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey90") +
      geom_point() +
      scale_color_manual(values = color_legend_Subtype) +
      labs(y = ylab, x = "Proliferation rate (70/doubling time)", color = "Subtype") +
      facet_wrap(~metabolite) +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  return(p)
}
```

Create for each omics layer and save to file.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 18/2.54
#| fig-width: 14/2.54

omics_layers <- names(omics_datasets)
for (omics_layer in omics_layers) {
  print(str_c("Plotting ", omics_layer))
  metabolomics <- omics_datasets[[omics_layer]]
  p_scatter <- scatter_metabolite_plot(metabolomics)
  #plot(p_scatter)
  p_violin <- violin_metabolite_plot(metabolomics)
  #plot(p_violin)
  save_plot(
    here(output_dir, str_c("Supplementary_Figure_3_", omics_layer, ".png")),
    plot = p_scatter,
    base_height = cm_to_inch(18),
    base_width = cm_to_inch(14))
  save_plot(
    here(output_dir, str_c("Supplementary_Figure_4_", omics_layer, ".png")),
    plot = p_violin,
    base_height = cm_to_inch(18),
    base_width = cm_to_inch(14))
}
```
